metadata.audience: English-speaking independent visitors, especially Shanghai extensions, 1–4 days
metadata.promise: Hangzhou is a change of tempo and attention: lake, mountain, tea, Buddhist landscape and Song-era urban imagination—not a Shanghai day-trip checklist.
metadata.commercial_boundary: Research and human-checked digital roadbook only. No booking, bundled travel, guiding, ticket resale or third-party experience sales.

source_policy.rule: All opening, ticket, transport, weather, tea activity and rail facts are dynamic and require a dated official check. Community reports identify traveller friction only.

modules.name: West Lake as a slow landscape
modules.question: How do I experience West Lake without treating it as a lap around a postcard?
modules.output_rule: Choose a season, a pace and one relation—water, hill, garden, city edge or morning/evening light; do not force the whole lake.

modules.name: Tea as landscape, labour and taste
modules.question: What does Longjing mean beyond buying tea or staging a ceremony?
modules.output_rule: Separate tea landscape, tea museum/learning, village walking, tea purchasing and a verified participatory experience.

modules.name: Buddhist mountain and sacred etiquette
modules.question: Does Lingyin fit this traveller, and how should it be approached?
modules.output_rule: Use a religion/nature/stone-and-mountain reading; verify access and do not treat worship as spectacle.

modules.name: Song imagination and water-town urbanity
modules.question: What makes Hangzhou more than a scenic lake?
modules.output_rule: Use Southern Song, canals, old streets and museums only through the visitor's actual cultural question.

modules.name: Wetland and quiet alternatives
modules.question: What should replace an over-crowded or weather-poor West Lake day?
modules.output_rule: Use Xixi or a museum/tea alternative after current conditions and purpose are checked.

modules.name: Contemporary Hangzhou and digital life
modules.question: Is there a present-day Hangzhou layer for a repeat visitor?
modules.output_rule: Use public urban/cultural observations; avoid company visits or stale commerce recommendations.

modules.name: Shanghai–Hangzhou pacing decision
modules.question: Is Hangzhou a day trip, an overnight, or a destination in its own right?
modules.output_rule: Evaluate usable hours, weather, rail friction and desired depth; default to overnight when landscape/tea/temple are central.

modules.name: Weather, mobility and seasonal friction
modules.question: Can this route survive heat, rain, crowds and hilly walking?
modules.output_rule: Build weather exits and shorter alternatives before output.

points.name: West Lake intention card
points.why_it_matters: West Lake has different meanings for a walker, photographer, garden reader, first visitor and someone wanting quiet; a generic circuit serves none well.
points.agent_use: Ask what the visitor wants to notice and how much walking they can absorb.

points.name: West Lake morning/evening decision
points.why_it_matters: Time of day changes crowd, heat and light more than adding a second landmark.
points.agent_use: Offer a time window only after current weather and transit check.

points.name: Longjing tea landscape decision
points.why_it_matters: Tea fields can connect landscape, seasonal agriculture and taste, but they are not a guaranteed harvest, ceremony or shopping experience.
points.agent_use: Ask whether the client wants walking, learning, purchase or participatory tea work; field-check current conditions.

points.name: Tea purchase boundary
points.why_it_matters: A roadbook can help a visitor ask better questions about tea, but cannot authenticate quality, price, provenance or seller claims.
points.agent_use: Offer purchase-risk literacy, not shopping endorsements.

points.name: China National Tea Museum decision
points.why_it_matters: A potentially clearer learning layer for visitors who want tea context but not a village/field outing.
points.agent_use: Verify access and current content; use as a purpose-based alternative.

points.name: Lingyin Temple / Feilai Feng decision
points.why_it_matters: A mountain-and-sacred landscape distinct from West Lake and tea; worth time only when religion, sculpture, mountain atmosphere or walking is genuinely central.
points.agent_use: Ask mobility, religion interest and crowd tolerance; verify current entry rules.

points.name: Buddhist etiquette card
points.why_it_matters: Sacred space needs quiet, photography restraint and respect; it is not a backdrop for content creation.
points.agent_use: State public etiquette before recommending any temple.

points.name: Southern Song / Hangzhou memory decision
points.why_it_matters: A cultural lens connecting Hangzhou's former capital status, water-city imagination and present tourism without forcing a history lecture.
points.agent_use: Ask whether history, urban form or literary imagination is the actual reason.

points.name: Hefang Street decision
points.why_it_matters: A legible old-street/commercial layer that can suit first-time visitors but may conflict with clients seeking less retail mediation.
points.agent_use: Make opt-in; do not call it inherently authentic.

points.name: Grand Canal / water-city alternative
points.why_it_matters: A way to read Hangzhou through movement, trade and water beyond the West Lake image.
points.agent_use: Use only after a field walk establishes a coherent public route.

points.name: Xixi Wetland decision
points.why_it_matters: A possible quieter ecological/water alternative when the traveller seeks wetlands and time rather than a compressed scenic circuit.
points.agent_use: Do not call it a generic backup; ask whether wetland landscape is actually desired.

points.name: Rain/heat recovery block
points.why_it_matters: Rain and humidity change lake, hill and tea walks; a protected learning/seated block keeps the route humane.
points.agent_use: Keep an uncommitted indoor/seated alternative until current conditions are known.

points.name: Contemporary Hangzhou public-life lead
points.why_it_matters: A research lane for digital culture, design and current urban life beyond a corporate-tech fantasy.
points.agent_use: No company/campus visit claims; field-check public-facing material first.

points.name: Shanghai day-trip decision
points.why_it_matters: A day trip can work for one carefully bounded lake/city layer, but not West Lake, tea, Lingyin and a relaxed return all at once.
points.agent_use: Ask hotel location, train tolerance and a single central purpose. Recommend overnight if two major layers matter.

points.name: Hangzhou overnight decision
points.why_it_matters: An overnight makes room for low-crowd timing and reduces the need to convert landscape into a transit challenge.
points.agent_use: Use when lake, tea and temple/old-city all matter; do not promise scenic conditions.

points.name: Shanghai–Hangzhou–Suzhou choice
points.why_it_matters: Suzhou is best for gardens/canals/craft density; Hangzhou is best for lake-mountain-tea-temple pace. The client should not be sent to both by default.
points.agent_use: Ask whether the traveller wants garden/canal refinement or landscape/tea/sacred mountain.

points.name: Arrival, payment and local movement
points.why_it_matters: The city starts with an actual station/airport arrival, data/payment, hotel location and a weather-aware movement plan.
points.agent_use: Ask the arrival mode/time and mobile payment/data readiness before Day 1.

points.name: Mobility / hills / stairs decision
points.why_it_matters: Lake circuits, temple terrain and tea villages have very different walking burdens.
points.agent_use: Do not call a route easy without date-specific field verification; offer fewer layers.

points.name: One-day Hangzhou core
points.why_it_matters: One landscape or cultural anchor plus a meal/recovery window is more credible than attempting the whole Jiangnan image in eight hours.
points.agent_use: Require one primary lens and preserve return margin.

points.name: Four-day Hangzhou depth
points.why_it_matters: Space for lake timing, tea, sacred landscape and water-city/ wetland alternatives without copying the same view repeatedly.
points.agent_use: Use depth to add variety and rest, not attractions per hour.

Trigger day-trip versus overnight decision.
Ask desired relationship and walking/weather tolerance.

Route to Lingyin/etiquette and mobility check.
Route to Song/water-city lens.
Route to canal/old-city/modern contrast candidates.
Choose lake, tea hills or wetland by actual landscape desire.
Ask light, weather and crowd tolerance.

Escalate terrain/stairs to human review.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you willing to stay overnight, or must this be a same-day return from Shanghai?
Do you want water/landscape, a slow walk, photography, garden detail or simply a contrast to Shanghai?
Are you interested in tea landscape, learning, buying tea, or a verified participatory experience?
Is the draw Buddhist art, mountain atmosphere, worship, or a quieter natural setting—and how are stairs/terrain for you?
Do you want gardens/canals/craft density or lake/mountain/tea/temple pace, and how many days do you truly have?
What weather, walking or stair threshold requires a shorter or indoor alternative?
Would you like a human-checked brief with official links while you make bookings directly?

output_guardrails: Never combine West Lake, Longjing and Lingyin into a default day-trip promise.
Never promise tea harvest, tea ceremony, tea quality, price or provenance.
Never treat sacred space or village residents as a performance.
Never publish live rail, ticket, weather, access or transport claims without dated recheck.
Never force both Suzhou and Hangzhou into a short Shanghai stay.
No booking, payment collection, packaging, guiding, transport or third-party experience sale.
